entries.title: Isaiah 51:1
segments: Hearken to me; the Messiah seems to be still the speaker.  Compare
.  The address is to God's people, who are thrice described by their character and relations to God, in

and thrice encouraged by the promise of God's everlasting faithfulness and love. 
 
  The rock--ye are hewn--the hole--ye are digged; that is, your origin, as explained in the next verse. 
 
vv 1-8. 
 
Heaven and earth are no so stable as the prosperity of the righteous: their helper and protector is the unchangeable God, who is faithful to fulfil all his promises to those who put their trust in him.

entries.title: Isaiah 51:2
segments: I called him alone; literally, "I called him one;" that is, when he was but one.  The power of God was shown by making of one man a great nation.

entries.title: Isaiah 51:5
segments: My righteousness; God's righteousness is manifested in the redemption of his people; hence, it is naturally joined with "my salvation."  So also

entries.title: Isaiah 51:6
segments: Lift up your eyes to the heavens; nothing is so stable as the heavens; yet these shall perish, while God's faithfulness to his people shall remain for ever.  Compare

entries.title: Isaiah 51:9
segments:
O arm of the Lord; the prophet calls upon God's arm to work as in ancient days. 
 
  Cut; hewn in pieces by thy plagues. 
 
  Rahab; Egypt.

The dragon; Egypt herself, under the symbol of the crocodile that inhabits the Nile. 
 
God is well pleased when his children urge his past interpositions for Zion as a reason why he should now deliver her: by every such interpostion he has pledged his infinite attributes to be with her, and help her, and give her the victory to the end of time.

entries.title: Isaiah 51:11
segments: Therefore the redeemed of the Lord shall return; thou shalt repeat thy wondrous works of old in bringing thy redeemed to thyself.

entries.title: Isaiah 51:12
segments:
vv 12-16. 
 
No array of human opposition, however formidable, ought to dismay God's people; they have on their side the Maker of heaven and earth, before whom the mightiest oppressors are but as chaff before the whirlwind.

entries.title: Isaiah 51:13
segments: Where is the fury of the oppressor? what has now become of it? This is said in anticipation of his destruction.

entries.title: Isaiah 51:14
segments: The captive exile hasteneth; the oppressor having been destroyed, the captive exiles whom he had imprisoned hasten to escape from their dungeon.

entries.title: Isaiah 51:16
segments: Plant the heavens--lay the foundations of the earth; the same as, "create new heavens and a new earth."

entries.title: Isaiah 51:17
segments: The cup of his fury; God's judgments are often compared to an intoxicating cup, which causes those who drink to reel.

entries.title: Isaiah 51:18
segments:
vv 18-20. 
 
When God would humble his people for their sins, he takes away from their leaders wisdom and strength, and leaves them no way of deliverance but that of a return to himself by repentance and renewed obedience.

entries.title: Isaiah 51:19
segments:
These two things; famine and the sword, producing desolation and destruction. 
 
  Who shall be sorry for thee--comfort thee? these words imply that Zion's griefs are beyond the reach of human sympathy and comfort. Therefore God himself will interpose to deliver and comfort her,

entries.title: Isaiah 51:21
segments:
vv 21-23. 
 
The sufferings which God inflicts upon his covenant people are designed for their purification, and he will in due time remove them.  But their merciless persecutors "shall have judgment without mercy."
